# Send a Message to a Channel (chat.postMessage)

## Prerequisites

- Your Slack app must have the required scope:
  - Bot token: `chat:write`
  - User token: `chat:write`
- The app/bot/user must have permission to post in the target conversation (and typically be a member of the conversation unless using `chat:write.public` for public channels).
- You must know the target conversation identifier to provide as `channel` (channel ID, channel name in limited cases, DM ID, MPIM ID, or a user ID to open a DM).

## Method

`POST`

## URL

`https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
```

## Description

Sends a message to a public channel, private channel, multi-person DM (MPIM), or direct message (DM/IM). You can send plain text, Block Kit blocks, and/or legacy attachments, and optionally post into threads.

> **When to use Block Kit vs plain text:**
> - **Use `blocks` (Block Kit)** for any message containing structured data, tables, multiple sections, headers, or rich formatting. Block Kit is the **recommended approach** for all non-trivial messages.
> - **Use plain `text` only** for simple, single-line notifications or fallback content.
> - **Always include `text`** as a fallback when using `blocks` — it appears in notifications, screen readers, and non-Block Kit surfaces.

## Enforcement Rules

- This endpoint has **no path parameters**.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Query Parameters** in the URL as query parameters and **not** in the body.
- The documentation states `token` can be sent as a POST parameter, but tokens should be passed via an HTTP Authorization header. **Do not include auth headers or auth fields in this knowledge file.**
- Content types supported by Slack: `application/json` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. This knowledge file uses `application/json`.

## Required Query Parameters

None.

## Optional Query Parameters

None.

## Required Request Body Fields

| Parameter | Type   | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `channel` | string | Channel identifier or destination. Can be an encoded ID or (in some cases) a channel name representing a public channel, private channel, MPIM, or IM/DM destination. # List Conversations (Channels) in a Workspace

## Prerequisites

- The calling app/token must have at least one of the required scopes for the conversation types you want to list:
  - `channels:read` (public channels)
  - `groups:read` (private channels)
  - `im:read` (DMs)
  - `mpim:read` (group DMs)
- To use `team_id`, the token must belong to an org-wide app; otherwise `team_id` is ignored.

## Method

`GET`

## URL

`https://slack.com/api/conversations.list`

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

## Description

Lists all channel-like conversations in a Slack workspace that the calling token has access to. The set of conversations returned depends on the token’s access and the `types` filter. Results are returned in pages using cursor-based pagination.

## Enforcement Rules

- **No path parameters** are used for this endpoint.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Query Parameters** in the URL query string, **not** in the body.
- Do **not** send authentication parameters (like `token`) in the query string or body in your final request (authentication is handled separately by the system).

## Optional Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | string | Pagination cursor. Set this to the `response_metadata.next_cursor` value from a prior response to fetch the next page. If omitted, fetches the first page. Example: `dXNlcjpVMDYxTkZUVDI=` |
| `exclude_archived` | boolean | If `true`, excludes archived channels. Default: `false`. Example: `true` |
| `limit` | number | Maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer **under 1000**. Default: `100`. Slack recommends no more than `200` at a time. Example: `20` |
| `team_id` | string | Encoded team ID to list channels in. **Required only** if the token belongs to an org-wide app. Ignored for workspace-level tokens. |
| `types` | string | Comma-separated list of conversation types to include. Any combination of: `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im`. Default: `public_channel`. Example: `public_channel,private_channel` |

## Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | boolean | Indicates whether the request succeeded. |
| `channels` | array | List of limited channel-like conversation objects. |
| `response_metadata` | object | Metadata for pagination. |
| `response_metadata.next_cursor` | string | Cursor

# Create One or More Pages

## Endpoint

`POST http://one-medley/v1/notion/create-multiple-pages`

## Description

Creates several Notion pages in one call. Each page is created in turn, a page failing does not stop the ones after it, and every result is reported at the index of the page it came from.

## Required Body Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `connectionKey` | string | The Notion connection to act as |
| `pages` | array | The pages to create, 1-100 of them. See below |

## Optional Body Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `parent` | object | Where a page that names no `parent` of its own is created |

### Each entry of `pages`

Notion's own create-a-page body, and nothing else - a field this does not declare is refused rather than dropped, because dropping one would create a page that is not the one you asked for and report it as a success.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `parent` | object | Where this page goes: `{"type": "data_source_id", "data_source_id": …}`, `{"type": "page_id", "page_id": …}`, and Notion's other parent shapes. Falls back to the call-level `parent` |
| `properties` | object | The page's properties, keyed by property name. Optional: a page created without them is untitled |
| `children` | array | Block objects to put in the page |
| `content` | array | Initial page content as block objects |
| `markdown` | string | The page's content as markdown |
| `icon` | object | `emoji`, `external`, `file_upload` or `custom_emoji` |
| `cover` | object | `external` or `file_upload` |
| `position` | object | Where the page sits among its siblings: `{"type": "after_block" \| "page_start" \| "page_end"}`, with `position.after_block` (a block id) required for the first. Notion's append-children endpoint takes a `position` too, but its enum is `after_block`, `start`, `end` - the two are not interchangeable |
| `template` | object | The template to create it from: `{"type": "none" \| "default" \| "template_id"}`, with `template.template_id` required for the last. `default` is refused unless this page's parent is a data source |

# Send Email

## Endpoint

`POST http://one-medley/v1/gmail/send-email`

## Description

Sends an email through Gmail. Takes the message as fields - recipients, subject, body - and assembles the RFC 2822 message Gmail's API requires, so the caller never builds MIME or base64.

Supports multiple recipients, CC and BCC, HTML or plain-text bodies, custom labels, and replying into an existing conversation via `threadId` with the `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers a standards-compliant client reads.

Plain-text bodies are escaped and wrapped in HTML, which avoids Gmail's plain-text line wrapping. A caller who already has HTML passes `isHtml: true` and it is sent as written.

## Request Body

### Required Request Body Fields

| Parameter       | Type               | Description                                                                  |
|-----------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `connectionKey` | string             | The connection key for Gmail authentication                                  |
| `to`            | string \| string[] | Recipient(s). A comma-separated string or an array                           |
| `subject`       | string             | Subject line. Non-ASCII subjects are RFC 2047 encoded automatically          |
| `body`          | string             | Body content. Plain text unless `isHtml` is set                              |

### Optional Request Body Fields

| Parameter    | Type               | Description                                                                                  |
|--------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `cc`         | string \| string[] | CC recipients                                                                                 |
| `bcc`        | string \| string[] | BCC recipients                                                                                |
| `isHtml`     | boolean            | Treat `body` as HTML and send it unescaped (default: `false`)                                  |
| `from`       | string             | The `From` header. Must be an address the account is allowed to send as                        |
| `replyTo`    | string             | The `Reply-To` header

# List a Calendar's Events

## Prerequisites

- You must know the target `calendarId`
- To access the authenticated user's primary calendar, you can use `primary` as the `calendarId`

## Method

`GET`

## URL

`https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{{calendarId}}/events`

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

## Description

Returns events on the specified calendar. This endpoint supports filtering, pagination, free-text search, incremental synchronization via `syncToken`, and repeated query parameters for event types and extended properties.

## Enforcement Rules

- The `calendarId` path parameter **must always be present**.
- If the user provides a `calendarId`, use that value directly.
- Do **not** call the API with a missing or empty `calendarId`.
- The special value `primary` is valid for the currently logged-in user's primary calendar.
- Always construct the path as `/calendars/{{calendarId}}/events`, where `{{calendarId}}` is a **non-empty string**.
- Do **not** infer or guess the `calendarId` beyond the user's input.
- When executing the action, ensure to send "Path Parameters" in the URL and not in the body.
- When executing the action, ensure to send "Query Parameters" in the URL as query parameters and not in the body.

### Valid Examples

```http
/calendars/primary/events
/calendars/user@example.com/events
/calendars/c_1883qf4v9j1abc123def456ghi@group.calendar.google.com/events
```

### Invalid Examples

```http
/calendars//events
/calendars/events
/events
```

## Required Path Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `calendarId` | string | Calendar identifier. To retrieve calendar IDs, call the calendar list endpoint. Use `primary` to access the currently logged-in user's primary calendar. Send in the URL path. |

## Optional Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alwaysIncludeEmail` | boolean | Deprecated and ignored. Send as a query parameter. |

# Create an Issue

## Prerequisites

- Access to a Linear workspace with permission to create issues in the target team
- A valid `teamId` to associate the new issue with

## Method

`POST`

## URL

`https://api.linear.app/graphql`

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
```

## Description

Creates a new Linear issue using the `issueCreate` GraphQL mutation. You provide the issue fields via the `input` object (at minimum, `teamId`) and specify which fields you want returned for the created issue in the GraphQL selection set.

## Enforcement Rules

- This is a GraphQL endpoint: send the mutation in the JSON request body under `query`, and pass inputs via `variables`.
- When executing, send **Path Parameters in the URL, not in the body** (not applicable; this endpoint has no path parameters).
- When executing, send **Query Parameters as URL query parameters, not in the body** (not applicable; this endpoint has no query parameters).
- The mutation requires `input` and `input.teamId` must be provided and non-empty.

## Required Path Parameters

None.

## Required Query Parameters

None.

## Required Request Body Fields

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | GraphQL mutation document. Must include `mutation issueCreate($input: IssueCreateInput!) { issueCreate(input: $input) { ... } }`. |
| `variables` | object | Variables map for the GraphQL operation. Must include `input`. |
| `variables.input` | object | The issue object to create. |
| `variables.input.teamId` | string | **Required.** Identifier of the team associated with the issue. |
